title: Strategic plan and lower natural gas rates
subtitle: Also: UW Innovation Arena small business space, noise exemptions, advisory committee terms of reference, and BIA board appointments.
overview: The Finance and Corporate Services Committee spent most of its meeting on the 2023-2026 Strategic Plan. It received the Resident Panel's final report for information, then recommended that Council approve the initial set of actions for the plan {{vote:m8}}. The plan has five goal areas: a connected city, a green city, an economically thriving city, a caring city, and stewarding a better city together. Staff said the actions are meant to be adjusted over the term rather than fixed for four years.

The committee also recommended up to $450,000 from the Economic Development Investment Fund 2.0 for leasehold improvements to a City-leased small business space in the University of Waterloo Innovation Arena {{vote:m9}}. It recommended lowering the natural gas supply rate for Kitchener Utilities system gas customers from November 1, 2023, while raising delivery rates slightly {{vote:m10}}. Staff said the net effect is a lower bill for the average residential customer.

On the consent agenda, the committee recommended approving terms of reference for the Committee of Adjustment and Property Standards Appeal Committee, appointments to the Belmont and Downtown Business Improvement Area boards, and four noise exemptions for fall events. All of these recommendations go to Council for final decision.

decisions.detail: The committee recommended that Council approve the initial set of actions in Appendix C of report CAO-2023-337 for the 2023-2026 Strategic Plan {{vote:m8}}.

The committee recommended cutting the Kitchener Utilities supply rate to 16.70 cents per cubic metre from 20.85 cents, approving the proposed delivery rates from November 1, 2023, and reviewing the supply rate quarterly.

The committee recommended allocating up to $450,000 from EDIF 2.0 for leasehold improvements at 280 Joseph St West, referring about $17,500 a year in common area costs to the 2024 budget process, and authorizing the lease.

decisions.item: Committee of Adjustment and Property Standards Appeal Committee terms of reference
decisions.detail: The committee recommended approving terms of reference for both bodies and adding them to the City's policy manual.
The committee recommended confirming board appointments to the Belmont and Downtown BIAs through November 14, 2026, and amending Chapter 70 to clarify the number of Downtown BIA directors.

decisions.item: Burning House Music Festival noise exemption
decisions.detail: The committee recommended a noise exemption for the September 16, 2023 event at the Bingeman Centre, with conditions including an 11 p.m. end, a 55 dBA limit and a pay-duty Noise Officer paid by the organizer.

debate: On the Committee of Adjustment terms of reference, one councillor asked for clearer meaning of a "minor" variance and how pecuniary interest applies when developers sit on the committee. Staff said the terms now bring members under the code of conduct and let them declare a perceived bias. Staff also said a zoning by-law amendment, not a variance, is the route for significant height or density increases.

Delegates from Compass Kitchener and resident panel members praised the panel process, saying in-person talks with staff, shared ground rules and reporting back on changes made it more than a rubber stamp. Compass Kitchener urged making the panel permanent. Councillors asked how the approach could be used for planning applications and the budget.

Councillors asked for changes to the plan's wording. One wanted active transportation routes described as connected, and another asked that the community grants action refer to community priorities, not city priorities. Staff said they would take both away before Council's final vote. Another councillor asked that the actions be viewed through equity, affordability, accessibility, environmental and reconciliation lenses. A councillor also asked why green development standards are labelled "new", and staff said the work is already underway at the regional level.

Delegates from the Active Transportation and Trails Advisory Committee supported the plan. They asked for closing gaps in the network, more bike and scooter parking, better wayfinding and safety. One delegate also urged planning for much higher energy costs, denser neighbourhoods and parking reform.

On the Innovation Arena space, councillors asked whether the City needed new space regardless, and staff said yes because the current location is only guaranteed until September 2025. Staff said the other municipalities are not contributing space. On gas rates, staff said the lower supply rate passes savings to customers, while delivery rates rise because of new locating regulations, higher costs from Enbridge and the energy transition plan.
